start.response: Trace one supplied quantity through three labelled IPO boxes, then change the input and ask which value changes.

values.risk: Text digits automatically behave like numbers, and every digit-only identifier should be converted.
values.response: Compare "4" * 3 with 4 * 3. Keep an identifier such as 0042 as text when its leading zeros carry meaning.

representation.risk: Changing notation changes the value, or every visible character occupies one byte.
representation.response: Convert a value back to decimal by place value; separately distinguish code point, encoding and stored bytes.

selection.risk: At least excludes equality, or every if branch executes.
selection.response: Predict below/at/above a threshold, mark the true condition, then trace exactly the chosen branch.

loops.risk: range includes its stop value, or an accumulator should reset on every iteration.
loops.response: Trace a zero-iteration case and a three-iteration case; place initialisation outside the repeated body and explain the stopping check.

functions.risk: Printing and returning are the same, or a definition executes its body immediately.
functions.response: Assign the result of a print-only function, inspect None, then compare a returned value and trace two separate calls.

arrays.risk: The final valid index equals the length, or an equal maximum should always replace the first match.
arrays.response: Label zero-based positions and specify first/last-match behaviour. Test empty, one-element and equal-value cases.

files.risk: Successful conversion proves domain validity, and a conversion handler handles every file failure.
files.response: Separate file opening, text conversion and range checking. Trace missing-file, blank-line, malformed and out-of-range cases.

design.risk: A running program or impressive theme proves that every requirement is met.
design.response: Trace each measurable requirement into a design decision and an expected/actual acceptance case. Use the shared core before optional presentation choices.

software-responsibility.response: Compare attribution and permission in a supplied licence case; require a short source/assistance record alongside the learner explanation.

networks.risk: An application protocol performs every communication job.
networks.response: Follow a message through application, transport, IP and local-link responsibilities. Ask for the mechanism as well as the name.

addressing.risk: An IP address, mask and gateway are interchangeable settings.
addressing.response: Calculate the network address, decide local/remote delivery, then justify the reachable gateway using the supplied prefix.

network-design.risk: A faster switch always fixes slow internet access, or a diagram enforces access policy.
network-design.response: Identify the bottleneck from supplied evidence and test both an allowed and a prohibited path against the proposed design.

network-review.risk: One symptom identifies one certain fault.
network-review.response: Ask for a hypothesis, competing explanation and smallest useful next observation. Keep observed results separate from inference.

consolidation.risk: Copying a corrected answer proves transfer.
consolidation.response: Retain the original attempt, explain the cause, then set a changed independent retry after a gap.

exam-preparation.risk: A definition answers every explain or justify command.
exam-preparation.response: Underline each command and subpart; connect a correct technical statement to the supplied case and its requested evidence.

database-foundations.risk: A plausible or faithfully copied value is necessarily true.
database-foundations.response: Distinguish domain validation, checking against a source and source accuracy/authenticity using a deliberately plausible wrong record.

entities-relationships.risk: A repeated description is a suitable primary key, or an M:N line alone implements the relationship.
entities-relationships.response: Use duplicate names/descriptions to challenge the key; resolve M:N with a junction and identify the whole key.

normalisation.risk: Normalisation is just deleting duplicate-looking rows.
normalisation.response: State dependencies and preserve every event while removing repeating groups, partial dependencies and transitive dependencies in order.

sql-basics.risk: SELECT changes stored columns, and storage order guarantees result order.
sql-basics.response: Compare the stored table before/after a projection; require ORDER BY with an explicit tie-breaker where needed.

database-solution.risk: A successful SQL execution message proves the right rows changed.
database-solution.response: Preview the target, predict the change, check the target and a non-target, and test an invalid record in a disposable copy.

security-threats.risk: Two knowledge secrets are two-factor authentication, or naming a control explains its effect.
security-threats.response: Classify factor categories and require a mechanism linking each proposed control to the stated threat.

responsible-data.risk: Replacing names with codes guarantees anonymity.
responsible-data.response: Test whether a mapping or contextual linkage can identify people, then justify minimisation, access and retention decisions.

unit2-review.risk: A content mapping is evidence of learner mastery.
unit2-review.response: Use a fresh database or scenario and collect the actual independent response; the map locates resources only.

unit2-consolidation.risk: Every low-confidence topic needs the same extra reading.
unit2-consolidation.response: Diagnose one concrete error first, select its matching explanation, then retest with changed data.

unit2-exam.risk: Memorised SQL can be applied without checking the schema or report grain.
unit2-exam.response: Read the keys and desired row meaning first; manually predict one included and one excluded row before writing the report.

unit3-fluency.risk: A loop form is interchangeable at the zero-iteration boundary.
unit3-fluency.response: Contrast pre-test, fixed-count and post-test reasoning for zero and non-zero cases before translating to the taught Python form.

unit3-structures.risk: A shallow copy recursively duplicates every nested object.
unit3-structures.response: Draw references for nested lists and dictionaries; change one nested value and predict every alias before running.

unit3-search.risk: Binary search works on any input order, or a failed search has no boundary cases.
unit3-search.response: State the sorted-range precondition; trace missing, first, last and repeated-key cases against the chosen match contract.

unit3-sort.risk: One pass means the whole list is sorted, or all sorts establish the same sorted region.
unit3-sort.response: Trace a first pass of bubble, insertion and selection sort and mark the invariant/sorted region after that pass.

unit3-objects.risk: A class is one shared instance, or aliases create independent object state.
unit3-objects.response: Construct two instances, change one through a method and predict which references observe the change.

unit3-inheritance.risk: A base-typed collection prevents overridden behaviour.
unit3-inheritance.response: Call the same method on mixed instance types; explain lookup and the shared contract, then compare inheritance with composition.

unit3-project.risk: A feature-rich engine or extra asset work substitutes for the required algorithm evidence.
unit3-project.response: Trace the core requirements to the year-level structures, algorithms and tests; require an individual explanation and changed code task.

unit3-reliability.risk: A passing component test proves user acceptance or a timing claim.
unit3-reliability.response: Separate component, integration, acceptance and defined-workload evidence; record actual conditions and limits.

unit3-network-models.risk: The bottom TCP/IP network grouping is identical to OSI network layer 3.
unit3-network-models.response: Compare the two model diagrams, map responsibilities and keep the course terminology explicit.

unit3-addressing.risk: A prefix length is a host count, or any starting address is an aligned subnet.
unit3-addressing.response: Calculate block size, network, broadcast and ordinary host range before allocating every interface, including the gateway.

unit3-secure-networks.risk: VLAN separation alone proves all inter-network access is blocked.
unit3-secure-networks.response: Mark routing and enforcement points and test a permitted and a denied service-specific path.

unit3-review.risk: A patch that matches one expected number proves the contract.
unit3-review.response: Use changed normal, empty, boundary and failure cases; check state and non-mutation rules as well as the visible output.

unit3-consolidation.risk: Immediate repetition of the same answer is a delayed independent retry.
unit3-consolidation.response: Change the stimulus and revisit after a gap; retain the date, original response and support used.

unit3-exam.risk: A faster algorithm is acceptable even if it violates order or mutation requirements.
unit3-exam.response: Read the function contract first and test any proposed optimisation against its output-order and state-change rules.

unit4-design.risk: Each component of a composite key must be unique alone, or documentation itself enforces integrity.
unit4-design.response: Use repeated components with unique pairs; compare the diagram/dictionary to actual primary, foreign and domain constraints.

unit4-sql.risk: SUM over a booking join gives session totals, and DISTINCT always repairs inflation.
unit4-sql.response: Declare the report grain and list the repeated source rows. Aggregate at the correct entity level before composing reports.

unit4-project.risk: One statement failure always undoes every earlier change, or ACID is merely a SQL keyword list.
unit4-project.response: Explain each ACID property using a logical operation; separately teach the chosen driver and transaction boundary before requiring implementation.

unit4-analysis.risk: An accepted account event identifies the person beyond doubt.
unit4-analysis.response: Distinguish event evidence from attribution and record plausible alternatives and the next justified observation.

unit4-controls.risk: Hiding an edit button enforces permissions, or logging prevents every change.
unit4-controls.response: Test the permission at the actual boundary; verify unchanged data after denial and demonstrate recovery separately.

unit4-crypto.risk: Encryption, hashing and signing all provide the same protection.
unit4-crypto.response: Match confidentiality, integrity and authentication needs to mechanisms and key roles; include the identity-binding and endpoint limits.

unit4-ethics.risk: Every entity has the same privacy obligations, or a suspected incident automatically meets a statutory threshold.
unit4-ethics.response: Identify entity, jurisdiction, date and supplied facts. Use current authoritative sources and explain the conditional judgement.

unit4-review.risk: A correct joined report proves schema, import, security and recovery readiness too.
unit4-review.response: Collect distinct evidence for each requirement and its relevant failure case; use the SQL pathway checklist to expose missing preparation.

unit4-consolidation.risk: A revision checklist tick is a grade prediction.
unit4-consolidation.response: Choose a concrete weak skill, collect an unaided changed response and record the remaining support or uncertainty.

unit4-exam.risk: A list of controls is a justified evaluation.
unit4-exam.response: Require a recommendation tied to the case, mechanism, evidence and limitations; check all command words and subparts.

programming.baseline: School-approved Python 3 editor, supplied synthetic files and a paper trace sheet. Use the general program or 2D task without specialist hardware.
programming.specialist: Drone commands/telemetry in Year 11 or a VR/spatial engine in Year 12, through a locally verified adapter and staged teaching.
programming.alternative: Use a text-only adapter, replayed synthetic telemetry, a 2D sprite or a paper state trace with the same declared contract.
programming.evidence: Paper/replay work supports algorithm reasoning. Actual Python execution is still needed for a programming practical; a trace does not prove flight, headset performance or live API integration.

networking.baseline: Printed logical diagrams, fictional addressing tables, synthetic frame/packet records and an offline calculation sheet.
networking.specialist: Network pods, managed switches/routers, wireless equipment and locally approved observation/configuration tools.
networking.alternative: Use supplied configuration snapshots, MAC/lease tables, request cards and fault logs; use an approved simulator if available.
networking.evidence: A model can demonstrate reasoning and predicted policy results. It does not establish actual cabling, live configuration or measured physical-network performance.

databases.baseline: A school-approved SQLite RDBMS on an ordinary computer, the four/six-table fixtures, dictionaries and query/result sheets.
databases.specialist: A local database server or server/pod integration with a declared DBMS, driver and access model.
databases.alternative: Use SQLite for actual database creation/manipulation; use printed base/changed records for prediction and manual joins before execution.
databases.evidence: Paper results are preparation, not proof of a working database or enforced constraints. A server alternative needs explicit dialect, types, transaction and parameter-placeholder teaching.

security.baseline: Fictional logs, role/policy tables, threat scenarios and expected/actual test records.
security.specialist: An authorised isolated pod/server lab and teacher-selected specialist demonstrations linked to a precise concept.
security.alternative: Use the offline policy model, synthetic logs and paper allowed/denied cases; keep the stimulus and reasoning demand comparable.
security.evidence: Predicted outcomes and actual observations must be labelled separately. A demonstration is not the same as each learner independently configuring or testing a system.

representation.baseline: Place-value cards, a supplied character/code-point table, pencil and optional Python verification.
representation.specialist: A supplied drone/VR telemetry record can provide a context after the representation concept is taught.
representation.alternative: Use fictional numbers and text records; no device, paid asset or particular encoding tool is necessary.
representation.evidence: Record the declared width, signed/unsigned interpretation and encoding. A correct numeric conversion does not by itself demonstrate every character-encoding concept.

planning.baseline: A written brief, requirement/test table, dependency chart, synthetic case cards and the general textbook examples.
planning.specialist: Use a drone, VR, pod or hackathon scenario as the local brief after prerequisites and assessment conditions are settled.
planning.alternative: Use a club-loan, booking-service or simple 2D/console scenario with equivalent conceptual requirements.
planning.evidence: Retain requirement-linked decisions, independent explanations and actual evidence where execution is required. More complex equipment does not itself demonstrate stronger understanding.

bridges.title: Drone programming, 2D hackathon and physical networking
bridges.status: Draft 64-entry Unit 1 lesson crosswalk available; equipment procedures and event/contact-hour budget still need local confirmation.
bridges.flow: General programming explanation -> predicted trace -> taught adapter/replayed telemetry -> expected/actual comparison -> changed textbook task. Later networking uses the same address/device/diagnostic concepts.
bridges.assessment: The proposed local applied-engine component and hackathon component belong to a reconciled local task architecture. The textbook standalone Pygame project is a separate example; do not add its workload or marks automatically.
bridges.alternative: Python text-only engine, synthetic telemetry and ordinary 2D project; supplied network evidence for conceptual work.
bridges.beforeIssue: Confirm adapter/runtime contract, observed versus simulated evidence, individual explanation/change task, component contributions and the event/exam calendar.

bridges.title: Pod/security scenarios and a relational database
bridges.status: SQL-strand weekly planning is available; a complete local security/cipher/privacy lesson crosswalk remains to be checked.
bridges.flow: General database/security reading -> supplied records or logs -> guided practice -> changed independent attempt -> feedback before the local practical.
bridges.assessment: If the practical is in Week 10, its SQL operations must be taught and practised earlier. Do not copy a plan that leaves first SELECT teaching until after the practical.
bridges.alternative: SQLite fixtures on ordinary computers; synthetic security cases and offline policy tests.
bridges.beforeIssue: Confirm assessed operations, normalisation/CREATE prerequisites, constraint tests, recovery evidence and any server-driver differences. Keep non-SQL content inside the same lesson budget.

bridges.title: VR/spatial OOP, advanced 2D hackathon and network performance
bridges.status: Concept/equipment bridge available; a full local 64-entry lesson crosswalk and timing trial are not yet completed.
bridges.flow: General objects/grids/dictionaries/algorithm explanation -> small ordinary Python example -> taught spatial/2D implementation -> individual state/algorithm explanation -> changed core task.
bridges.assessment: Retain the proposed applied VR engine plus hackathon relationship as a local option. Vendor APIs, coordinate dimensions, rendering and first-use integration require their own preparation if retained in the task.
bridges.alternative: Ordinary Python classes and a 2D scene or console model; synthetic timings/network traces.
bridges.beforeIssue: Confirm the actual supported runtime/API, platform language bridge, accessible alternative, independent authentication and total project/event time. A headset outcome does not replace algorithm evidence.

bridges.title: Database/application integration and security on pods/servers
bridges.status: SQL-strand weekly planning is available; full local integration/security lesson mapping and workload trial remain pending.
bridges.flow: General multi-table/schema/ACID/security concept -> SQLite practice -> explicitly taught driver/server adaptation -> requirement-linked test, recovery and justified evaluation.
bridges.assessment: Core ACID concepts remain syllabus-linked. Explicit driver/transaction syntax and supporting LEFT JOIN/HAVING material need teaching before they are required by a local task.
bridges.alternative: SQLite plus an ordinary Python application, fictional booking data, local role/policy models and paper analysis.
bridges.beforeIssue: Verify driver placeholders, data types, transaction boundaries, constraints/cascade behaviour, import decisions and actual recovery tests; do not infer equivalence from successful connection alone.
